editorial.headline: Where Recreational Fishing Becomes a Managed Business
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the places, waters and supporting services that turn recreational and sport fishing into an organised offering—and it remains open to PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Fishing is the main event here, but the activity is broader than a single pond or shoreline. It covers the operation of places and facilities designed primarily for fishing, across freshwater settings such as rivers, estuaries, lakes, beaches, archipelagic waters and fishing ponds, as well as saltwater settings from shallow onshore waters to offshore sea. The commercial proposition may be recreational fishing or sport fishing; what matters is that the operator is providing the setting in which the activity takes place.

That setting can be practical, social and guided. The scope expressly includes recreational fishing-guide services, alongside supporting services such as food and beverages. In other words, the activity can hold together the physical fishing environment, the visitor experience and the ancillary hospitality that makes a day on the water—or at a managed fishing pond—work as a coherent operation. It is an activity open at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales, allowing the business model to be registered across the full scale range stated in the record.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward: the activity is open, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. There is no lower national foreign-ownership ceiling recorded for it. That clarity matters because Bali applies a permanent, island-wide PMA restriction to activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk. The local position for this activity, however, does not turn that rule into a prohibition.

For Bali, the record places the decisive point at the Large scale: its OSS risk is Medium-High/High, and it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Put plainly, a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today; the provincial moratorium does not bar it. The national openness and the Bali outcome are aligned here, but the Bali conclusion rests on the recorded risk position at Large scale—not on an invented exemption or a separate ownership condition.
